items.text: Train your children in the essential values of human life, including a correct attitude of freedom with regard to material goods and a simple and austere lifestyle.
items.quote: parents must trustingly and courageously train their children in the essential values of human life

items.text: Enrich your children with a sense of true justice and true love, as sincere solicitude and disinterested service, especially to the poorest and most in need.
items.quote: a sense of true love, understood as sincere solicitude and disinterested service with regard to others, especially the poorest and those in most need

items.text: Practice self-giving in your relationships with brothers and sisters, modeled on the love of husband and wife.
items.quote: the self-giving that must be practiced in the relationships between brothers and sisters

items.text: Practice self-giving toward elder generations in the family, as the self-giving love of husband and wife is the model.
items.quote: the self-giving that must be practiced in the relationships between brothers and sisters and the different generations living together in the family

items.text: Give your children a clear and delicate sex education that is truly and fully personal.
items.quote: parents called to give their children a clear and delicate sex education

items.text: Carry out your children's sex education under your attentive guidance, whether at home or in educational centers chosen and controlled by you.
items.quote: must always be carried out under their attentive guidance, whether at home or in educational centers chosen and controlled by them

items.text: Educate your children in chastity, developing their authentic maturity and respect for the nuptial meaning of the body.
items.quote: education for chastity is absolutely essential, for it is a virtue that develops a person's authentic maturity

items.text: Bring your children to a knowledge of and respect for moral norms as the necessary guarantee for responsible personal growth in human sexuality.
items.quote: education must bring the children to a knowledge of and respect for the moral norms as the necessary and highly valuable guarantee for responsible personal growth in human sexuality

items.text: Devote special attention and care to education in virginity or celibacy as the supreme form of self-giving.
items.quote: Christian parents, discerning the signs of God's call, will devote special attention and care to education in virginity or celibacy as the supreme form of that self-giving
items.conflict: Conflicts with 1 Cor 7:7-9, 38; Heb 13:4: celibacy is a gift, not a state superior to marriage.

heading: IV - PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY IN DIFFICULT CASES · 77 · Particular Circumstances

items.text: Remain faithful to your spouse through long years, so that your married love may deepen in old age.
items.quote: In old age married love, which has been increasingly purified and ennobled by long and unbroken fidelity, can be deepened.

items.text: Do not abandon or neglect your aged parents; do what you can to relieve their loneliness.
items.quote: the burden of loneliness, more often psychological and emotional rather than physical, which results from abandonment or neglect on the part of children and relations.

items.text: When family members are divided over faith, keep dialogue alive and freely show love and respect.
items.quote: dialogue with the other party must always be kept alive. Love and respect must be freely shown.

heading: IV - PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY IN DIFFICULT CASES · 84 … Those Without a Family

items.text: Bring up your children in the Christian faith.
items.quote: bring up their children in the Christian faith

items.text: If you cannot separate for serious reasons, live together in complete continence, abstaining from acts proper to married couples.
items.quote: they "take on themselves the duty to live in complete continence, that is, by abstinence from the acts proper to married couples."
items.conflict: Binds consciences beyond Scripture; Scripture permits remarriage after divorce for marital unfaithfulness and teaches the marriage debt (Matt 19:9; 1 Cor 7:3-5).

items.text: Help the divorced and do not let them consider themselves separated from the Church.
items.quote: help the divorced, and with solicitous care to make sure that they do not consider themselves as separated from the Church

items.text: Show great understanding and willingness to help those who have no natural family.
items.quote: families, which must show great understanding and willingness to help

heading: IV - SHARING IN THE LIFE AND MISSION OF THE CHURCH · 64 · To Discover the Image of God in Each Brother and Sister

items.text: Daily promote a truly personal community between you, initiated and fostered by an inner communion of love.
items.quote: through a daily effort to promote a truly personal community, initiated and fostered by an inner communion of love

items.text: Let the family's welcome, respect, and service shape daily life within the family, honoring each person as a child of God.
items.quote: It should be so especially between husband and wife and within the family

items.text: Welcome, respect, and serve every human being, considering each one's dignity as a person and as a child of God, and place the family at the service of the human person and the world.
items.quote: The Christian family welcomes, respects and serves every human being, considering each one in his or her dignity as a person and as a child of God.

items.text: In the poor, the weak, the suffering, and the unjustly treated, discover the face of Christ and serve them, attending to the image of God and offering what you give to Christ.
items.quote: In each individual, especially in the poor, the weak, and those who suffer or are unjustly treated, love knows how to discover the face of Christ.

items.text: Form your children in love and practice love in all your relationships, keeping the family open to the community, moved by justice and concern for others.
items.quote: Another task for the family is to form persons in love and also to practice love in all its relationships

heading: III - PARTICIPATING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOCIETY · 42 · The Family as the First and Vital Cell of Society … Society at the Service of the Family

items.text: Respect and foster the personal dignity of each family member; practice free giving through acceptance, dialogue, availability, service and solidarity.
items.quote: free giving takes the form of heartfelt acceptance, encounter and dialogue, disinterested availability, generous service and deep solidarity.

items.text: Help the younger generation grow wiser and harmonize personal rights with the requirements of social living.
items.quote: the various generations come together and help one another to grow wiser and to harmonize personal rights with the other requirements of social living.

items.text: Be the first school of the social virtues for your children.
items.quote: it is within the family that they find the first school of the social virtues.

items.text: Practice hospitality; open your home and heart to welcome the brother or sister in need.
items.quote: Practice hospitality... welcome the brother or sister in need.

items.text: Devote yourselves to social service, especially for the poor and for those whom public welfare cannot reach.
items.quote: can and should devote themselves to manifold social service activities, especially in favor of the poor.

items.text: Be the first to see that the State's laws and institutions do not offend but support and positively defend the family's rights and duties.
items.quote: see that the laws and institutions of the State not only do not offend but support and positively defend the rights and duties of the family.

items.text: Do not take away from families the functions they can perform themselves; instead favor and encourage their responsible initiative.
items.quote: The State cannot and must not take away from families the functions that they can just as well perform on their own or in free associations.

items.text: Ensure families have all the economic, social, educational, political and cultural assistance they need.
items.quote: the public authorities must do everything possible to ensure that families have all those aids—economic, social, educational, political and cultural assistance—that they need.

heading: PART FOUR · PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY: STAGES, STRUCTURES, AGENTS AND SITUATIONS · I - STAGES OF PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY · 66 · Preparation for Marriage

items.text: Teach your children from early childhood the values of marriage and family life through a gradual process of education.
items.quote: the families themselves that, according to ancient customs, ensure the passing on to young people of the values concerning married and family life

items.text: Give them wise family training from early childhood, helping them know their own personality, strengths, and weaknesses.
items.quote: wise family training which leads children to discover themselves as being endowed with a rich and complex psychology and with a particular personality with its own strengths and weaknesses

items.text: Instill in them esteem for all authentic human values, formation of character, control of inclinations, and right regard for the opposite sex.
items.quote: esteem for all authentic human values is instilled, both in interpersonal and in social relationships, with all that this signifies for the formation of character

items.text: Give them solid spiritual and catechetical formation showing that marriage is a true vocation and mission.
items.quote: solid spiritual and catechetical formation that will show that marriage is a true vocation and mission

items.text: Do not exclude the possibility of total self-gift to God in the priestly or religious life.
items.quote: without excluding the possibility of the total gift of self to God in the vocation to the priestly or religious life
items.conflict: Monastic vows and clerical celibacy are not commanded; 1 Cor 7:9 permits marriage.

items.text: Prepare them for life as a couple: present marriage as an interpersonal relationship to be continually developed, and teach conjugal sexuality and responsible parenthood with essential medical and biological knowledge.
items.quote: present marriage as an interpersonal relationship of a man and a woman that has to be continually developed

items.text: Acquaint them with correct methods for the education of children and help them gain stable work, sufficient financial resources, sensible administration, and notions of housekeeping.
items.quote: acquaint those concerned with correct methods for the education of children, and will assist them in gaining the basic requisites for well-ordered family life

items.text: As a household, be involved in the different phases of your children's preparation for marriage.
items.quote: The Christian family and the whole of the ecclesial community should feel involved in the different phases of the preparation for marriage

heading: IV - PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY IN DIFFICULT CASES · 78 · Mixed Marriages … 80

items.text: Ensure, as far as possible, the Catholic baptism and upbringing of your children in the Catholic faith.
items.quote: the consequent obligation to ensure, as far as is possible, the Baptism and upbringing of the children in the Catholic faith.
items.conflict: Reformed teaching: raise children in the true gospel, not Roman Catholic doctrine.

items.text: Respect your spouse's religious freedom: do not pressure them to change their beliefs or obstruct their religious practice.
items.quote: by undue pressure to make the partner change his or her beliefs, or by placing obstacles in the way of the free manifestation of these beliefs by religious practice.

items.text: Train your child from childhood to master concupiscence and to form relationships of genuine love.
items.quote: from childhood, with the help of Christ's grace and without fear, has been trained to dominate concupiscence from the beginning and to establish relationships of genuine love with other people.

items.text: Let your marriage be indissoluble; do not enter a trial union.
items.quote: between two baptized persons there can exist only an indissoluble marriage.

heading: IV - SHARING IN THE LIFE AND MISSION OF THE CHURCH · 57 · Marriage and the Eucharist … Educators in Prayer

items.text: Celebrate and live your marriage within the Eucharist, drawing your covenant from Christ's sacrifice of love for the Church.
items.quote: marriage normally be celebrated within the Mass... The Eucharist is the very source of Christian marriage.

items.text: Repent and grant mutual pardon within the bosom of the family, and have recourse together to God's mercy in the sacrament of Penance.
items.quote: Repentance and mutual pardon within the bosom of the Christian family... receive their specific sacramental expression in Christian Penance.

items.text: Pray together in common as husband and wife, offering your family life to God in thanksgiving, petition, and trust.
items.quote: Family prayer has its own characteristic qualities. It is prayer offered in common, husband and wife together, parents and children together.

items.text: Pray together with your children; your example and living witness of prayer is fundamental and irreplaceable.
items.quote: The concrete example and living witness of parents is fundamental and irreplaceable in educating their children to pray.

items.text: Educate your children in prayer, introducing them to the mystery of God and teaching them to know, worship, and love God and neighbor.
items.quote: Christian parents have the specific responsibility of educating their children in prayer... children should be taught... to have a knowledge of God, to worship Him and to love their neighbor.

items.text: Teach your children Christian prayers and prepare them for the sacraments of Confession, Communion, and Confirmation.
items.quote: Mothers, do you teach your children the Christian prayers? Do you prepare them... for the sacraments... Confession, Communion and Confirmation?

items.text: Pray with your children and your whole domestic community, and join your example of honesty in thought and action to common prayer.
items.quote: And you, fathers, do you pray with your children, with the whole domestic community... Your example of honesty in thought and action, joined to some common prayer...

items.text: Encourage sick children to invoke the aid of the Blessed Virgin and the saints, and say the family rosary together.
items.quote: invoke the aid of the Blessed Virgin and the saints... Do you say the family rosary together?
items.conflict: Prayer to Mary and the saints conflicts with Christ as sole mediator (1 Tim. 2:5).

heading: CONCLUSION · 86
II - STRUCTURES OF FAMILY PASTORAL CARE … Associations of Families for Families

items.text: As a married couple, witness by a life lived in conformity with the divine law in all its aspects.
items.quote: through the witness of a life lived in conformity with the divine law in all its aspects

items.text: Give them Christian formation, help them mature in faith, educate them in chastity, and prepare them for life.
items.quote: through the Christian formation of the children, through helping them to mature in faith, through education to chastity, through preparation for life

items.text: Guard them from ideological and moral dangers.
items.quote: through vigilance in protecting them from the ideological and moral dangers

items.text: Lead them gradually and responsibly into the ecclesial and civil community, and help and advise them in choosing a vocation.
items.quote: through their gradual and responsible inclusion in the ecclesial community and the civil community, through help and advice in choosing a vocation

items.text: Help one another toward human and Christian growth together.
items.quote: through mutual help among family members for human and Christian growth together

items.text: Do works of spiritual and material charity toward families in need and toward the poor, the sick, the old, the handicapped, orphans, widows, abandoned spouses, and mothers-to-be in difficulty.
items.quote: towards the poor, the sick, the old, the handicapped, orphans, widows, spouses that have been abandoned, unmarried mothers and mothers-to-be

heading: IV - PASTORAL CARE OF THE FAMILY IN DIFFICULT CASES · 81 … 83

items.text: Do not remain in a free union; enter into a true and proper marriage with your partner.
items.quote: smooth the path for them to regularize their situation

items.text: Do not keep your children in a free union, because cohabitation can damage them psychologically.
items.quote: possible psychological damage to the children

items.text: If you are married only civilly, make your marriage a religious marriage in the Church.
items.quote: induce them to regularize their situation in the light of Christian principle
items.needs_role: Catholic in a merely civil marriage

items.text: Do not separate until you have tried every reasonable means of reconciliation; let separation be your last resort.
items.quote: Obviously, separation must be considered as a last resort, after all other reasonable attempts at reconciliation have proved vain.

items.text: If separated, preserve fidelity to your spouse and do not enter a new union.
items.quote: so that they can preserve their fidelity even in their difficult situation

items.text: Forgive your spouse and remain ready to return to your married life.
items.quote: cultivate the need to forgive which is inherent in Christian love, and to be ready perhaps to return to their former married life.

items.text: If civilly divorced, devote yourself to carrying out your family duties and the responsibilities of Christian life.
items.quote: devote themselves solely to carrying out their family duties and the responsibilities of Christian life
items.needs_role: civilly divorced person who has not remarried

items.text: If civilly divorced, do not enter a new union while your first spouse lives.
items.quote: refrain from becoming involved in a new union
items.conflict: Matthew 19:9 permits the innocent party after biblical divorce to remarry.
items.needs_role: civilly divorced person who has not remarried

heading: IV - SHARING IN THE LIFE AND MISSION OF THE CHURCH · 61 · Liturgical Prayer and Private Prayer … The New Commandment of Love

items.text: Introduce your children to the liturgical prayer of the whole Church, preparing them for it and extending it into personal, family and social life.
items.quote: serve as the natural introduction for the children to the liturgical prayer of the whole Church

items.text: Join with the household in the gradual participation in the Eucharist, especially on Sundays and feast days, and in the other sacraments.
items.quote: gradual participation by all the members of the Christian family in the celebration of the Eucharist, especially on Sundays and feast days

items.text: Ensure your children are gradually initiated through the sacraments of Christian initiation.
items.quote: particularly the sacraments of Christian initiation of the children

items.text: Take part with your household in the common recitation of the Divine Office.
items.quote: it recommends the recitation of the Divine Office in common

items.text: Celebrate at home the times and feasts of the liturgical year in a way suited to each member.
items.quote: strive to celebrate at home, and in a way suited to the members, the times and feasts of the liturgical year

items.text: Lead your children in morning and evening prayers, in reading and meditating on the word of God, in preparation for the sacraments, and in grace before and after meals.
items.quote: Apart from morning and evening prayers, certain forms of prayer are to be expressly encouraged

items.text: Pray the family rosary with your children, so that the family gathering becomes a time of prayer and devotion to Mary.
items.quote: the rosary should be considered as one of the best and most efficacious prayers in common that the Christian family is invited to recite
items.conflict: Prayer to Mary in the rosary conflicts with Christ as sole mediator (1 Tim. 2:5).

items.text: Honor the Blessed Virgin Mary as the Mother of Christian families and of domestic churches, and imitate her interior spiritual attitude.
items.quote: she who is the Mother of Christ and of the Church is in a special way the Mother of Christian families, of domestic Churches
items.conflict: Venerating Mary as mother of Christian families ascribes to her a role Scripture gives to Christ alone.

items.text: Live by the evangelical law of love that the Spirit engraves on your hearts in Matrimony, in responsible freedom.
items.quote: marriage sets forth anew the evangelical law of love, and with the gift of the Spirit engraves it more profoundly on the hearts of Christian husbands and wives

items.text: With your household, practice devotion and consecration to the Sacred Heart of Jesus as an encouraged form of prayer.
items.quote: devotion and consecration to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
items.conflict: Consecration to a physical symbol of Christ's heart is an extra-biblical devotion; worship must be by Scripture alone.
